flaws.title: One-for-zero reward accounting can checkpoint rewards on an uninitialized end tick
flaws.sequence:
1. A top-of-block one-for-zero swap in `AngstromL2.afterSwap` moves a pool from `startTick` up to `endTick = E`, where `E` is an exact multiple of the tick spacing but has no initialized liquidity, and there is at least one initialized tick strictly between `startTick` and `E`.
2. `AngstromL2._oneForZeroDistributeTax` creates or reuses a `TickIteratorUp` through `initUp(..., startTick, E)` / `reset(startTick)`.
3. `reset` only filters out an uninitialized `endTick` once, immediately after its own first `_advanceToNextUp(self)`. After later `getNext()` calls consume real initialized ticks below `E`, the next internal `_advanceToNextUp` can still stop with `currentTick == E` even though `E` is uninitialized.
4. `AngstromL2._oneForZeroCreditRewards` then treats `E` as a crossed tick: it executes `rewards[ticks.poolId].rewardGrowthOutsideX128[tickNext] += cumulativeGrowthX128`, and `getTickLiquidity(E)` contributes zero liquidity delta.
5. The rewards state now contains a checkpoint for a tick that was never initialized/crossed; later reward accounting for liquidity added or removed with boundary `E` reads polluted outside-growth data and can overpay or underpay LP rewards.
flaws.impact: Reward accounting can be written to an uninitialized tick. That can misattribute swap-tax rewards for later LP positions using that boundary, letting some LPs receive rewards they did not earn or shorting honest LPs.
